text:
incident-bot: SEV-2: Streaming route /v1/stream - sustained stall/chunking delays -> p95 up from ~400ms to 6.2s, p99 spiking to 19.4s. Error rate (502/504) + connection resets increasing. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/streams?range=15m. Paging @alex (oncall)

alex (oncall): ack — I'm on it. grabbing logs + running repro now.

alex (oncall): quick repro from my laptop: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood/v1/stream?demo=1"` — client hangs after first chunk, then long pause, then more chunks. Seeing long gaps (10-15s) between chunks locally.

maria (sre): I can see backlog on proxy layer. connection queue lengths and `write` stalls. nginx proxy_socket stats show send queue growth. Also seeing many `CLOSE_WAIT` on proxy nodes in region eu-west-1.

lee (infra): any deploys to the streaming-proxy cluster in last 24h?

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: streaming-proxy:release-2026.03.12 at 2026-03-12T08:14:05Z by chen. No rollback.

chen (eng): that release included a default `proxy_buffering` change to improve throughput for normal HTTP but I flagged SSE as a potential mismatch. PR: https://git.redwood/streaming/proxy/pull/438

alex (oncall): log excerpt from proxy when stall occurs:
```
[2026-03-12T09:02:12Z] conn=12 write=0/65536 blocked for 15321ms upstream=api-01
[2026-03-12T09:02:12Z] client_reset: broken pipe
```
Looks like proxy tries to buffer but client isn't reading.

maria (sre): hypothesis: proxy buffering + slow/paused clients => large proxy write buffers leading to head-of-line stalls; chunking gets delayed until buffer flush conditions met.

alex (oncall): plan: 1) attempt safe mitigation on a narrow canary (disable buffering for SSE location), 2) if good, roll to rest of proxies, 3) if not, fallback to short polling for heavy customers.

lee (infra): I'm creating a canary config patch now. will apply to 2/24 nodes in eu-west-1.

lee (infra): Applied canary: `location /v1/stream { proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; }` reloaded nginx on canary nodes.

alex (oncall): canary metrics after 3 minutes: p95 -> 720ms (from 6.2s), p99 -> 640ms (from 19.4s), error rate normalized. Nice. Rolling to remaining nodes.

chen (eng): note: we should include `proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive"` / ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Also consider reduce `proxy_buffers` default size and add per-connection write-backpressure metric.

alex (oncall): rolling deploy to rest of cluster now (eu-west-1, us-east-1). Restarting proxies gracefully to avoid client disconnect storms.

alex (oncall): roll complete. Global metrics show p95 back to ~430ms, p99 ~800ms. Some residuals but much improved.

jordan (pm): customer impact: how many customers saw degraded streams and for how long? any paid customers affected?

support-bot: 7 active customers reported streaming interruptions; 3 had auto-failover to polling in their SDKs and saw degraded UX for 8-20 minutes. No data loss reported. Ticket IDs: #3421 #3423 #3427. Top affected customer: AcmePayments (session ids logged).

alex (oncall): confirmed: AcmePayments had multiple reconnects and 504s between 09:00-09:18 UTC. We proactively reached out to their AE and sent timeline.

maria (sre): temporary mitigation done. Next actions (post-incident):
- Add automated detection for rising proxy write queue and alert at threshold
- Add per-connection write-backpressure metric and dashboard
- Default SSE config: `proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_buffers 4 8k;` in streaming location
- Add client SDK guidance for backpressure-aware read loop and automatic reconnect jitter
- Run load tests with slow/paused consumers to validate buffering interaction

chen (eng): created PR to enforce SSE config by default + instrumentation: https://git.redwood/streaming/proxy/pull/441. Includes Nginx metric exporter changes (proxystat write_queue).

alex (oncall): handing off to @maria (sre) for follow-up and postmortem. Summary: SEV-2 due to proxy buffering interaction with slow consumers after recent proxy config change. Mitigated by disabling buffering on SSE endpoints and rolling config. Customer impact limited to transient UX degradation for ~7 customers.

maria (sre): ack — I'm taking ownership. Will open a postmortem doc, link to PRs, and schedule a postmortem review. Action items assigned and ETA for fixes: 48h for metrics, 72h for default config PR review/merge.

alex (oncall): thanks all — leaving notes in runbook and incident channel. If any regressions, ping paging again. :thumbsup:

maria (sre): quick note for runbook update:
```
- When SSE stalls observed: verify proxy_buffering and chunked transfer settings
- Canary change procedure: apply to 10% nodes, monitor p99 for 5m, then roll 25% -> 50% -> 100%
- If canary fails: revert config and enable customer polling fallback
```

alex (oncall): handing off at 10:20 UTC. All open ops tasks listed in the postmortem doc. Good job team.

maria (sre): closing thread; will post postmortem link here when ready.
